steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState from 'react' here

// Your component will go below
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement for React and useState is added at the top of the file.
successCriteria: The code includes a valid import statement that imports both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the import statement needs adjustment. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App with proper TypeScript typing. The component should return a JSX element.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function named App that returns JSX. In TypeScript, you can specify the return type as JSX.Element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional App component is defined with TypeScript typing, ready to be filled with accessibility content.
successCriteria:
The code defines a component named App that returns JSX (even if just a placeholder like
).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component is named App and returns JSX with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component definition is missing or incorrect. Create a functional component named App that returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize state for form data
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useState hook to initialize a state variable called formData. It should be an object with name and email properties, both initially empty strings.
steps.hint: Use useState with a generic type to specify the shape of formData. For example: useState<{ name: string; email: string }>({ name: '', email: '' })
steps.expectedOutcome: The formData state variable is initialized with an object containing empty string values for name and email properties.
successCriteria: The code includes a useState call that declares formData and setFormData, with an initial value of { name: '', email: '' } and proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the formData state with proper TypeScript typing. This gives you a structured way to track user input in your accessible form.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your TypeScript typing or initial values. Make sure formData is an object with both name and email properties as empty strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on this single step: initialize formData state using useState with { name: '', email: '' } as the initial value. Remember to include TypeScript typing for the state.

steps.title: Initialize state for form submission status
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, initialize a new state variable called 'isSubmitted' with an initial value of false, using the useState hook.
steps.hint: You'll need to call useState<boolean>(false) and destructure the returned array into isSubmitted and setIsSubmitted.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing a boolean state variable
const [isSubmitted, setIsSubmitted] = useState<boolean>(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a new state variable 'isSubmitted' that tracks whether the form has been submitted, initialized to false.
successCriteria: The code should include a call to useState<boolean>(false) that returns an array destructured into isSubmitted and setIsSubmitted, placed inside the App component after the formData state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the isSubmitted state variable. This will allow us to track form submission status and provide appropriate accessibility feedback.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState<boolean>(false) and destructuring the array into both isSubmitted and setIsSubmitted inside the App component.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on initializing the isSubmitted state. Use the useState hook with a boolean type and false initial value, then destructure the result into two variables.

steps.title: Define handleInputChange handler
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function named handleInputChange that takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter and updates the formData state.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses setFormData to update the state based on the input's name and value from the event.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleInputChange function that properly updates the formData state when called with an input change event.
successCriteria: Function uses setFormData to update state
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a typed event handler that will update your form state correctly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your handler: 1) Has the correct parameter type, 2) Uses setFormData to update state, and 3) Accesses the name and value from event.target.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function called handleInputChange that takes an event parameter and updates the formData state using setFormData.

steps.title: Define handleSubmit handler
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function called handleSubmit that takes a React.FormEvent parameter, prevents the default form submission behavior, and sets isSubmitted state to true.
steps.hint: Create a function that accepts an event parameter of type React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>, calls event.preventDefault(), and then calls setIsSubmitted(true).
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleSubmit function is added to the component that prevents default form submission and updates the submission status.
successCriteria: The code should include a handleSubmit function that: 1) Accepts a React.FormEvent parameter, 2) Calls event.preventDefault(), 3) Calls setIsSubmitted(true).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handleSubmit function with proper accessibility considerations by preventing the default form submission behavior.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your handleSubmit function: 1) Accepts a React.FormEvent parameter, 2) Calls event.preventDefault(), 3) Calls setIsSubmitted(true).
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleSubmit function is missing or doesn't meet the requirements. It should prevent default form submission and update the isSubmitted state.

steps.title: Return the main container with proper semantic structure
steps.instruction: In your component's return statement, replace the existing <div> with a <main> element that has role="main" and contains an <h1> heading with the text 'Accessible Contact Form'.
steps.hint: Use the <main> element instead of <div> for the main content container. Add role="main" for explicit ARIA semantics. Include an <h1> as the first child inside <main>.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will return a semantic <main> container with proper ARIA role and a heading, establishing an accessible document structure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've established proper semantic structure with <main> and a heading, which helps screen readers understand your page layout.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you use <main> with role="main"? Did you include an <h1> with the correct text?
steps.feedbackWrong: This step requires replacing the <div> with a semantic <main> element containing a heading. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Add the form element with accessibility attributes
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your App component, add a <form> element with the following accessibility attributes: 1) onSubmit handler connected to handleSubmit, 2) aria-label describing the form's purpose, and 3) role="form" for explicit semantic identification.
steps.hint: Add the form element directly inside the existing <div> container. Remember to use the handleSubmit function you defined earlier for the onSubmit event.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form element will be added with proper accessibility attributes and connected to the submit handler.
successCriteria: Form element exists with opening and closing tags
aria-label attribute is present with descriptive text
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an accessible form element with all required attributes. This ensures screen readers can properly identify and describe the form.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the form element, but some accessibility attributes are missing. Check that you have: 1) onSubmit connected to handleSubmit, 2) aria-label with descriptive text, and 3) role="form".
steps.feedbackWrong: The form element wasn't added correctly. Make sure to add a <form> element inside the <div> with the required accessibility attributes.

steps.title: Add name input with label and accessibility features
steps.instruction: Inside the form element, add a labeled text input for the name field. Include a label element with 'Name' text, an input element with type='text', name='name', value={formData.name}, onChange={handleInputChange}, and required attribute.
steps.hint: Use the <label> element with htmlFor attribute matching the input's id. Connect the input's value to formData.name and onChange to handleInputChange.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have a properly labeled text input for the name field with accessibility features and connected to the existing state and handler.
successCriteria: The code must include: 1) A <label> element with text content 'Name' and htmlFor attribute, 2) An <input> element with type='text', name='name', value={formData.name}, onChange={handleInputChange}, and required attribute, 3) Both elements placed inside the form.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an accessible name input with proper labeling, value binding, and event handling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but some accessibility features or connections are missing. Make sure you have: a label with 'Name' text and htmlFor, an input with type='text', name='name', value={formData.name}, onChange={handleInputChange}, and required attribute.
steps.feedbackWrong: The name input isn't properly set up. Remember to create a labeled text input with all required accessibility attributes and connect it to the existing formData state and handleInputChange handler.

steps.title: Add email input with label and accessibility features
steps.instruction: Inside your form element, add a labeled email input field with proper accessibility attributes. The input should have: 1) A label with text 'Email' and proper htmlFor attribute, 2) An input element with type='email', name='email', value bound to formData.email, onChange handler, required attribute, and appropriate ARIA attributes.
steps.hint: Follow the same pattern as the name input but use type='email' and name='email'. Remember to bind the value to formData.email and use the existing handleInputChange handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of accessible email input
<label htmlFor='email'>Email</label>
<input
  type='email'
  id='email'
  name='email'
  value={formData.email}
  onChange={handleInputChange}
  required
  aria-required='true'
  aria-label='Email address'
/>
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have a properly labeled email input field with all required accessibility attributes, bound to the formData.email state.
successCriteria: Label element with htmlFor='email' and text 'Email'
Input has at least one ARIA attribute (aria-required or aria-label)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an accessible email input with proper labeling, value binding, and ARIA attributes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but some accessibility features are missing. Make sure you have: a label with htmlFor='email', input type='email', name='email', value={formData.email}, onChange={handleInputChange}, required attribute, and at least one ARIA attribute.
steps.feedbackWrong: The email input doesn't meet accessibility requirements. Please add a labeled email input field with proper ARIA attributes, bound to the formData.email state using the existing handleInputChange handler.

steps.title: Add submit button with accessibility attributes
steps.instruction: Inside your form element, add a submit button with type='submit', appropriate ARIA attributes, and wire it to your existing handleSubmit function.
steps.hint: Use the <button> element with type='submit'. Add aria-label for screen readers and ensure it's properly connected to the form submission.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of an accessible submit button
<button 
  type="submit" 
  aria-label="Submit the form"
  onClick={handleSubmit}
>
  Submit
</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have a properly accessible submit button that triggers the form submission.
successCriteria: Connected to handleSubmit via onClick or form onSubmit
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added an accessible submit button with proper ARIA attributes and event handling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your button has type='submit' and appropriate accessibility attributes.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding a <button> element inside the form with type='submit' and accessibility features.

steps.title: Add submission feedback with accessibility considerations
steps.instruction: Add conditional rendering after the form to display submission feedback when isSubmitted is true, using an ARIA live region for accessibility.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator or logical && to conditionally render a paragraph or div with aria-live="polite" and role="status".
steps.expectedOutcome: After the form, a message appears when the form is submitted, announced to screen readers via an ARIA live region.
successCriteria: Conditional rendering based on isSubmitted state
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added accessible feedback that will be announced to screen readers when the form is submitted.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added conditional feedback, but check that it includes proper ARIA attributes like aria-live="polite" and role="status".
steps.feedbackWrong: The submission feedback is missing or doesn't meet accessibility requirements. Ensure it conditionally renders when isSubmitted is true and includes ARIA live region attributes.
